text.text: Track every roof from first call to final payment. Jobs move across the board, the crew foreman sees their own list under Mine, and Mark done closes the job after the final walk. Materials shows the yard stock; Invoices shows who has not paid.

Overdue roof jobs
My roof jobs
Overdue invoices
Speed wins roofing leads. Send the estimate within two days of the inspection.
On the roof
Photograph every slope, vent, flashing point and any damage.
Measure the area in squares and record the pitch.
Note the decking condition and anything hidden.
Back at the office
Price materials from the yard list, then labor hours at the crew rate.
Add dumpster, permit and overhead lines.
Send the estimate with photos and two options when it makes sense.
A full replacement should finish in one to two days. Prepare the day before.
The day before
Confirm delivery of shingles and the dumpster.
Check the forecast and move the job on rain.
Text the customer the crew start time.
On the day
Tarp landscaping and protect the attic.
Strip, deck check, underlayment, flashing, shingles, vents, cleanup.
Foreman photographs each stage and enters hours.
After a storm the phones ring for a week. Triage, not panic.
Triage
Emergency tarps for open roofs first.
Then leaks, then inspections.
Mark each call with a priority and a date.
Staying fair
Never promise insurance outcomes. Offer to meet the adjuster and share your photos. Keep prices the same as before the storm.
